digest.description: Digest of the current managed resources

helmChartUrl.description: URL of the helm chart deployed

releaseName.description: The helm release name this composition resolved to, written by every phase that resolves it. It exists so that RESOLUTION and PERSISTENCE can be told apart from the object alone. The krateo.io/release-name label is write-once, so an established composition carries it and resolution short-circuits; a new or recreated composition has no label, and whether the resolved name was then persisted was NOT observable -- the openstack-ironic-operator-kog session could only infer it by counting 'Adopting the existing helm release' log lines (11 on a probe against 0 in production), because managedFields is stripped on these objects (zero entries on the probe AND zero on a production object that demonstrably carries the label, so ownership said nothing). With this field the three states read directly: label present means it was read from the label and no adoption ran; label absent with releaseName present means adoption resolved it and the write landed; label absent with releaseName absent is the 2.13.61 defect -- resolved in memory and never persisted. NO DEFAULT, DELIBERATELY. Nine of the twelve baseline fields omit one, and here it is load-bearing rather than incidental: a `default: ""` makes the apiserver materialise the key on every composition, which collapses the third state into the second and destroys the only distinction the field is for. Absence must stay absence.

helmChartVersion.description: Version of the helm chart deployed

managed.description: List of the managed resources installed by the helm chart

apiVersion.description: API version of the managed resource

path.description: Path of the managed resource, you can use this path to ask the API server for the resource

managedDigest.description: Digest of the helm release that status.managed was decoded FROM, stamped by the phases that record the inventory (#273). Observe compares it against the current release's digest to answer whether the recorded set is still the inventory of what is rendered — status.digest tracks the CURRENT release because Observe rewrites it every reconcile, while status.managed tracks whatever Create/Update last decoded, and nothing else ties the two together. MUST BE DECLARED HERE: a structural CRD schema prunes fields it does not declare, and while this was missing the cdc wrote it on every reconcile, the apiserver stripped it, and the absent-stamp branch reported drift forever — 502 drift reports across 30 of 30 inventoried compositions in 20 minutes on a fresh cluster (#293). Same failure as observedGeneration below.

observedGeneration.description: The .metadata.generation this status was produced from. The cdc writes it on every successful reconcile (unstructured-runtime SetObservedGeneration), but a structural CRD schema PRUNES fields it does not declare — so while this was missing, the write was silently stripped by the apiserver on every reconcile and the field read as permanently absent. Anything using it as a health signal therefore saw a false stall forever.

previousDigest.description: Digest of the previous managed resources

previousManagedCount.description: How many children status.managed listed BEFORE the last render replaced it, so the Ready message can say the recorded set shrank (#230). A multi-component bump legitimately renders fewer resources mid-flight; the rollup then evaluates the smaller set, finds it healthy and reports Available, and 122 -> 108 -> 122 is otherwise indistinguishable from 122 -> 122. Persisted rather than compared in flight because Observe stamps the message on every reconcile and has no previous inventory of its own. MUST BE DECLARED HERE for the same reason as managedDigest (#293).

managedChildrenCount.description: How many children status.managed currently lists. The denominator for healthEvaluatedChildren and unreadableChildrenCount, written on every rollup so that full coverage reads as an equality rather than as an absent field.

healthEvaluatedChildren.description: How many of the managed children this controller could actually health-evaluate. Less than managedChildrenCount means the Ready condition asserts something about a subset.

unreadableChildrenCount.description: How many managed children this controller's ServiceAccount was REFUSED a read of (HTTP 403). Non-zero is a gap in the generated RBAC, not a problem with the children; the child names are in the Ready condition message.

unrefreshedFields.description: The status paths (each statusDataTemplate forPath, exactly as declared) whose field holds a value that this reconcile's projection did NOT write: the mapping produced no output (e.g. `// empty`) or failed, so the value is whatever an earlier pass left. Written on every projection, an empty list included; absent means no projection ran (paused, or no statusDataTemplate). A field written as null is not listed. Read it with ApiResolved: under ApiPartiallyResolved it names the fields a failed RESTAction stage left stale.

unevaluatedChildren.description: Why the managed children that could not be health-evaluated were not, counted by cause. Every cause is written on every rollup, zero included. The counts sum to managedChildrenCount minus healthEvaluatedChildren minus unreadableChildrenCount. None of them changes Ready; they say what to do about a composition at Ready=Unknown/ZeroEvidence.

noReadyCondition.description: Children that publish no Ready condition (no conditions, or conditions without Ready) and have no kind-specific mapping. Actionable with a readiness projection on the CompositionDefinition (apiRef plus statusDataTemplate).

assertedReady.description: Children whose Ready=True was asserted, not observed (reason AssumedUpToDate: a rest-dynamic-controller kind declaring neither get nor findby). A question for the kind's RestDefinition.

notObserved.description: Children whose own controller could not observe the external resource (Ready reason NotObserved or ObserveFailed). Usually an outage or a credential problem on that child.

noEvidenceBelow.description: Children that are themselves at Ready=Unknown/ZeroEvidence: the missing evidence is in their own children.

helmOperation.description: The helm operation this composition's controller is running, written BEFORE every helm write that can leave the release locked pending-* (install, upgrade, a reconcile's real upgrade, rollback, uninstall) and removed when the operation returns (#461). It exists so the next controller can tell an operation still IN FLIGHT from one whose starter DIED (killed at a version handover, OOM, node loss): helm labels both pending-* and never re-labels a crash, so without this the next controller waits the full pending grace (16m) before rolling back. It is acted on only when it provably belongs to the pending revision (startedAt just before the release's LastDeployed) and its startedBy pod is NotFound; anything else keeps the grace. NO DEFAULT: absent means no operation recorded.

phase.description: install, upgrade, reconcile, rollback or uninstall.

startedAt.description: When the controller recorded the operation, immediately before calling helm.

startedBy.description: The name of the controller pod that started it (POD_NAME, from the downward API).

returnedAt.description: When the controller's call for this operation RETURNED with an error, leaving helm's lock behind (#497). Written only on that path. A record carrying it describes an operation that is provably no longer in flight, so the next controller clears the lock at once instead of waiting the pending grace. Absent while the operation runs, and on a record from a controller that predates it (then the grace applies, as before).

startedByProcess.description: The process that started the operation, distinct across container restarts in the same pod: a record naming this pod but another process belongs to a process that is gone (the container restarted), so its pending release is orphaned.

installFailures.description: The consecutive attempts of this composition's FIRST install that failed (#636), with the last error. Written when an attempt fails, read by Ready (InstallFailing from the 3rd), and removed once a revision is deployed. An interrupted attempt is not a failed one and does not count: status.installRecovery.count, which is cumulative, counts the automatic retries of both. The last error is readable here while a retry is running. NO DEFAULT: absent means none failed.

installRecovery.description: The last time this composition's controller retried its interrupted or failed FIRST install by itself (#629, #636), and how many times it has in all. Written before the retry's first deletion, kept after it succeeds, and never reset: a non-zero count says the chart's install hooks may have run more than once. The attempt counter that caps the retries of an interrupted install is the annotation krateo.io/interrupted-install-reinstalls, not this. NO DEFAULT: absent means it never happened (or happened under a CRD that predates this field, which prunes it).

kind.description: Retried: the interrupted or failed install was installed again over what it had created, with every install hook. The only value today; a consumer must accept others.

count.description: How many failed or interrupted attempts were retried over the composition's life. A retry a pass recorded and could not start counts once, however many passes repeat it.

reason.description: What the last retry was of: Interrupted or Failed, one token.

message.description: The same for a person, naming the revision.

revision.description: The helm revision the last retry was of. Removed once a revision is deployed.
